name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+11) in a majority-Black Mississippi Delta seat
Bennie Thompson's long incumbency and roughly 13-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage
Republican Ron Eller's minimal fundraising ($64K raised) with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Thompson's win odds near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+11 lean combined with Thompson's incumbency, dominant fundraising, and absence of any serious outside investment against him all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at roughly 97% win probability. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late influx of outside spending against Thompson or unusually high GOP turnout in a strong Republican-cycle environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson seeks another term in a western Mississippi district that leans strongly Democratic and has reelected him repeatedly by wide margins. His opponent, Republican Ron Eller, has run a minimally funded campaign, reporting about $64,000 raised and $38,000 on hand, while Thompson holds roughly $1.4 million. An independent candidate trails far behind in resources.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Thompson about a 97% chance of winning. With the incumbent unscathed by outside spending and the challenger lacking the money to change the dynamic, the seat is rated Safe Democratic, with Thompson expected to win by roughly 20 points.
